伊波家.name: Iha-ya
伊波家.desc: A shop in Nodake, Ginowan City, bustling with local customers. The Iha-ya soba has a combined broth with slightly pronounced pork bone, thick chewy straight noodles, and a nice accent of fuchiba (mugwort). With a complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), inari, or similar, the volume is outstanding.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
Iha-ya
Menu
Menu
I went into this shop at lunchtime, and it was quite bustling with local customers 😄　It feels like it's loved by the locals lol
From the menu, I decided to order the “Iha-ya soba,” which shares the shop's name.
Iha-ya soba, large　¥800
First, a sip of the soup. It's a combination of bonito and pork bone, a soup with slightly pronounced pork bone.
Iha-ya soba, large　¥800
Next, I taste the noodles 😆　The noodles are a thick straight type, chewy and just plain delicious.
The toppings include fuchiba (mugwort) too, which is a nice accent 😄　The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth tender, but they felt slightly sinewy.
As a complimentary item you can choose one from jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), inari, rice, or mini curry, and this time I ordered inari, but there was a lot of soup too, and I got full.
Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious, and there's plenty of volume. It seems popular with local customers too, so how about trying this shop once?

麺処 まんねん.name: Mendokoro Mannen
麺処 まんねん.desc: A shop of real skill with a ramen-like approach where you can choose the soup from 3 kinds: salt, soy sauce, or miso. The chicken-broth-based salt soup is fragrant with sesame oil, and the toppings are chicken breast and melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). A bowl where you feel new possibilities for Okinawa soba.
t: *This article was created with Claude 3.7 Sonnet AI and partially edited by me.
I went to eat here in November 2024 😄

I have the goal of touring every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, and I'm eating my way through little by little. I'm still far from conquering every shop, but this time I'll introduce “Mendokoro Mannen” in Nakanishi, Urasoe City 😊
Mendokoro Mannen
Mendokoro Mannen

“Mendokoro Mannen” is located a little way in from National Route 58 in Nakanishi, Urasoe City. The exterior is an ordinary soba shop, but when I went inside and looked at the menu, I noticed it has a feature different from other Okinawa soba shops. Believe it or not, like a ramen shop, you can choose from 3 kinds of soup: “salt,” “soy sauce,” and “miso”! 😲
Menu
Menu (the yushi soba is served with salt or soy sauce soup 😄)
Menu (the vegetable soba is served with salt, soy sauce, or miso-flavored soup 😄)
Menu
Menu

This is interesting. I'd previously eaten Okinawa soba with miso soup at “Nagomi” in Nago City, so I was going to go with miso soup this time too, but a staff member told me “The salt soup is recommended,” so I obediently switched to salt soup.

Looking at the menu, in addition to the signature “Mannen soba,” there's also “vegetable soba.” It seems you can choose salt, soy sauce, or miso for both. Moreover, at the top of the menu there was an explanation that they had changed from pork belly to chicken breast. Pork is the standard for Okinawa soba, but chicken is an interesting new attempt too 🐔
Inside the shop
Inside, there are counter seats and table seats; it's simple but clean. On the tables were condiments such as house-made kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) and shichimi.
It's Okinawa soba, not ramen, so there's kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) too 😆
Mannen soba, medium? (salt) ¥900? (sorry, I forgot the details 🙏)
The “Mannen soba (salt)” I ordered has arrived! Visually, there's chicken breast, chopped green onions, and the distinctive red fish cake (kamaboko), vivid in a clear soup 😄

First, a sip of the soup. Hm? This tastes more like ramen soup than Okinawa soba! It's a salt soup based on chicken broth, and I can taste the flavor of sesame oil too. There's not much of the pork bone flavor typical of Okinawa soba, but this is delicious in its own way 😋
Mannen soba, medium? (salt) ¥900? (sorry, I forgot the details 🙏)

Next, I have the noodles. Medium-thin noodles with a loose wave, a smooth texture with a slight chewiness, and I wondered, are these house-made fresh noodles? They go well with the soup and cling to it properly.

The topping, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), has a light seasoning and is simmered melt-in-your-mouth tender. The chicken breast, which replaced the pork belly, also surprisingly suits this soup and didn't feel out of place. The combination of the salt soup's refreshing taste and chicken actually feels natural.
What I suddenly thought after finishing was, “Next time I'd like to try the miso soup too.” I got curious, wondering what Okinawa soba with miso soup tastes like.

I felt that “Mendokoro Mannen” is a shop that, while protecting the tradition of Okinawa soba, is pursuing new possibilities for Okinawa soba by adding the options of salt, soy sauce, and miso. It's a creative type of Okinawa soba, but I think it's a dish worth trying at least once 😊

Rating (10.5/15): An Okinawa soba shop with distinctive soups you can choose from salt, soy sauce, or miso. This time's salt soup tasted more like ramen than Okinawa soba, but I enjoyed it as delicious in its own way. The noodles were smooth with a moderate chewiness, and the toppings were cooked tender too. It's recommended for people who want to enjoy a new variation of Okinawa soba!

読谷山そば.name: Yuntanza Soba
読谷山そば.desc: A hidden gem in Furugen, Yomitan Village, loved by local customers. An elegant bonito broth soup, medium-thick wavy noodles, and light, tender soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). There's a wide menu, including sea lettuce (āsa) and fuchiba (mugwort) soba.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with parts edited and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in January 2025 😁😊　At “Yuntanza Soba,” a hidden gem in Furugen, Yomitan Village, I had a bowl loved by local regulars. 📍
Yuntanza Soba
Yuntanza Soba's guide sign

Looking only at the exterior, it has a slightly plain appearance, but when you go inside, a more comfortable space than you'd imagine spreads out before you. It's an Okinawa soba shop with the kind of atmosphere where local customers never stop coming. It's shops like this that serve truly delicious Okinawa soba.

Inside the shop

What I ordered this time was the “soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba.” Looking at the menu, there's quite a rich variety, from half soba to meat soba, soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba, sea lettuce (āsa) and fuchiba (mugwort) soba, and so on. Being able to get a large serving of noodles for an extra ¥100 is a nice point for people with big appetites. 😋
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba　¥950

First, a sip of the soup. A deep taste with plenty of bonito broth spreads in my mouth. It's never too strong; rather, it's an elegant finish that makes you feel the quality of the ingredients. With this soup, it's so delicious you'll want to drink it all.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba　¥950

The noodles are medium-thick and wavy. They look soft, but with one bite, the way they cling to the soup is the best. The balance of chewiness and softness is kept perfectly, and the texture when you slurp them is irresistible. You can enjoy the goodness of both the parts soaked with soup and the center that retains a little firmness at the same time. ✨

And above all, the “soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki).” Soki has a strong image of bone-in pork, but the soki here is finished on the light side. There's certainly a little sinewy texture, but they're mostly tender.

The soup, noodles, toppings, every element was beautifully balanced, a bowl that made me think again, “Ah, so this is Okinawa soba.” With the contrast to the look of the building, I can see why locals come here so often. Just plain delicious, and nothing more is needed. 🌟

The price is reasonable too, and if you can eat soba of this level, it's a shop I definitely want to drop by whenever I come to Yomitan Village. It's a shop I can truly recommend to Okinawa soba lovers.

Rating (12/15): I thought this shop is also a high-level Okinawa soba shop with a good balance of noodles, soup, and toppings. When you come to Yomitan Village, how about trying it at least once? It's recommended 😄

田舎 読谷店.name: Inaka Yomitan-ten
田舎 読谷店.desc: A Miyako soba and soki soba specialty shop in Uechi, Yomitan Village. With outstanding value at ¥550 for Miyako soba, it's the traditional Miyako soba style where lean pork hides under the noodles. The plain, nostalgic, semi-outdoor shop makes you feel like you've slipped back in time to old Okinawa.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partially edited by me 😁
“Inaka Yomitan-ten” in Uechi, Yomitan Village. I went to eat here in August 2024 😄
Inaka Yomitan-ten

The shop's exterior truly has the feel of the “countryside” (inaka). The sign at the entrance has “Inaka” written in big letters, promoting “soki soba.” There's also an old vending machine on the premises, giving it a somehow nostalgic atmosphere.
Inside (outdoors?)
The menu posted inside the shop

When you go inside, a plain interior spreads out before you, with wooden tables and chairs lined up reminiscent of an old-fashioned Okinawan shokudo. There are several notices on the walls, and the one that catches the eye is the notice “Due to a pork shortage, the number of soki pieces has been reduced.” You can tell they're making all sorts of efforts to maintain cost performance.

Prices have been going up and up recently, but it's nice that at this shop you can enjoy delicious soba at the reasonable price of ¥550. The “soki soba” is offered at the same price too, so I think it's a shop that's quite easy on the wallet.
From the menu, I chose “Miyako soba” 😆
Miyako soba ¥550 (it's cheap (^0^;))

The “Miyako soba” has been brought out. The first thing that jumped out at me was its simple visual. Thin noodles are neatly arranged in a pale soup, with just two round fish cakes (kamaboko) on top. At a glance it seems there are few toppings, but actually the lean pork hidden under the noodles is the tradition of Miyako soba 😄
Miyako soba ¥550 (when I searched under the noodles, I found the lean pork lol (^0^;))

First, when I take a sip of the soup, the pork bone flavor spreads through my whole mouth, and within it I can sense a faint sweetness. I think this soup has a taste different from other Miyako soba. Although it's a pork-bone-based soup, it's characterized by a somehow gentle taste.

The noodles are thin and straight, soft yet with chewiness / bite, and they go perfectly with the soup. The lean pork is a bit firm and a sinewy texture remains, but you can enjoy how the flavor increases each time you chew it.

“Inaka Yomitan-ten,” which serves soba of this quality at a price of ¥550, has unbeatable cost performance. I think it's the perfect shop for when you want to enjoy delicious Okinawa soba quickly. That said, if you're looking for something special, it might be a bit lacking. But I think the appeal of this shop is, above all, its plainness and nostalgia. It makes you feel as if you've slipped back in time into an old Okinawan scene.

Rating (9/15): This time's “Miyako soba” gets a rating of ☆3, with the soup, noodles, and toppings all feeling ordinary. It's by no means bad; rather, I think it's a dish you can be satisfied with, given this taste at this price range. It reminded me of “Takoyaki Champon” in Okinawa City, which also has outstanding cost performance. A meal at this shop isn't especially luxurious, but I think it makes you feel a warmth that warms your heart. It's the kind of place I'd like to casually drop by again 😊

沖縄そばと郷土料理 島時間.name: Okinawa Soba to Kyodo Ryori Shima Jikan
沖縄そばと郷土料理 島時間.desc: A shop in Onna, Onna Village, in an old-folk-house style with red tiles that recreates a Ryukyuan house. In the interior with Okinawan folk songs as background music, you can enjoy island soba (shima soba) with plenty of bonito broth and local dishes. A shop where you can feel the Okinawan vibe when you come to Onna Village sightseeing.

Okinawa Soba to Kyodo Ryori Shima Jikan
